::: {#thm-one-sample-t-null}
#### Null distribution of the one-sample t statistic

Let $X_1, \ldots, X_n$ be independent,
each Gaussian with mean $\mu_0$ and variance $\sigma^2$, with $n \ge 2$.
Then the statistic $T \eqdef (\bar X - \mu_0) / (S / \sqrt{n})$
of @def-one-sample-t-test,
computed from these random variables,
has the $t_{n-1}$ distribution.
:::

::: proof

We use a standard fact about Gaussian samples [@hoggtanis2015]:
$\bar X$ and $S^2$ are independent,
and $V \eqdef (n-1) S^2 / \sigma^2$ has the $\chi^2_{n-1}$ distribution.
Also, $Z \eqdef (\bar X - \mu_0) / (\sigma / \sqrt{n})$
has the standard Gaussian distribution,
and $Z$ is independent of $V$ because $\bar X$ is independent of $S^2$.
So by @def-t-dist, $Z / \sqrt{V / (n-1)}$ has the $t_{n-1}$ distribution,
and this ratio equals $T$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{Z}{\sqrt{V/(n-1)}}
&= \frac{(\bar X - \mu_0) / (\sigma / \sqrt{n})}{\sqrt{S^2 / \sigma^2}}
&& \text{(substitute $Z$ and $V$)}\\
&= \frac{(\bar X - \mu_0) / (\sigma / \sqrt{n})}{S / \sigma}
&& \text{($\sqrt{S^2} = S$, since $S \ge 0$)}\\
&= \frac{\bar X - \mu_0}{S / \sqrt{n}}
&& \text{(the factors of $\sigma$ cancel)}\\
&= T.
\end{aligned}
$$

:::

::: notes
When the observations are not Gaussian,
$T$ still has approximately the standard Gaussian distribution
when $n$ is large,
<!-- Repoint to pds (limit-theorems.qmd#sec-clt) once it is published. -->
by the [central limit theorem](https://morrison-lab.github.io/rme/chapters/probability.html#the-central-limit-theorem),
and then $t_{n-1}$ is close to the standard Gaussian distribution
(@exm-t-dist).
:::
